summary: The batch is safe on length, mostly clean on brands, and has good single lines (wallet turning up in the fridge, treasure chest lock the key gave up on, delivery box arriving on the right birthday, ring swallowed by a fish, box turned into a rocket/car/castle/robot, mascara panda photos, grocery bags living with their hundred friends). Its biggest problem is the Legendary: 78 of 94 use the banned 'has done X for N years / still has its original or first X / never once' formula, so the top rarity reads as long-service certificates. Second, many Rares and Epics are competence or wholesome success ('kept X safe', 'nobody smudged', 'kept the picnic cold', 'fixed every broken thing'), and Epics lean on 'worn by every X at the Y / with a hundred others'. Third, the near-identical clusters share premises almost line for line: waist bags (belt/bum/fanny pack: snack pocket, 'kept essentials safe', festival/theme park/marathon crowd Epics, 'still has X from the first trip' Legendaries); coolers (cool box/cooler/ice chest 'kept it cold' Epics); cash box and donation box; cufflink and cufflinks (the lost partner, wedding glitter); ring and wedding ring (both slip off in the washing-up); keepsake, storage, cigar and tin boxes ('kept the family's memories'); umbrellas ('keeps dry/cool' at three rarities). Each issue says which side to change. Names are swapped or rotated on camera bag, cooler, cufflinks, duffel bag and pipe, and the matches Epic name describes the Rare. Child safety: the matches Rare, Epic and Legendary celebrate lighting candles, lanterns and a campfire, and nearly copy w09 lighter/zippo; replacements keep matches on the high shelf. Other flags: 'Captain Crunchwell' echoes a cereal mascot; 'Class Pet Election' pulls the ballot box towards politics; near-copies of w07 (badge pin prick on sewing box and brooch, scarf/wool length on bead, chain mail jingle on anklet, high-heel red carpet on lipstick, sun-hat shade on patio umbrella, kilt/hat/derby heirloom Legendaries); Ultimates that repeat the Epic name plus Daze/Finale, some promising stun where no variant stuns. Move mechanics are otherwise respected well: drain, heal, buff and multi-hit names match.

patterns.pattern: Legendary formula: 'Has done X for N years / for N generations / still has its original or first X / never once'. The lessons ban this; it turns the top rarity into a long-service certificate with no achievement or punchline.
patterns.suggestion: Replace each with one concrete outrageous achievement plus a punchline (see per-id issues). Rotate mechanisms: misplaced helpfulness, physics gone wrong, petty revenge, deadpan reaction. Never start more than a handful of Legendaries in a batch with 'Has'.

patterns.pattern: Epic crowd formula: 'worn/used by every X at the Y at once', 'every X in the room glittered', 'with a hundred/thousand others'. The same frame recurs across jewellery, bags and coins.
patterns.suggestion: Give each Epic one specific disruption with a consequence (soup diving, tablecloth yanked, sun cream over the queue) instead of multiplying the object.

patterns.pattern: Wholesome-success Rares and Epics: the object does its job very well ('kept X safe', 'nobody smudged', 'kept the picnic cold', 'fixed every broken thing'). Rare should be a troublesome power; Epic large-scale chaos.
patterns.suggestion: Turn competence into trouble: the cool box blows a winter wind, the tool bag swallows tools, the storage box swaps its contents.

patterns.pattern: Monster names sit on the wrong rarity (names written as a list, lore reordered).
patterns.suggestion: Re-pair per the per-rarity name issues before approval.

patterns.pattern: Near-identical object clusters share premises: waist bags (belt/bum/fanny: snack pocket, 'kept essentials safe', crowd Epics, 'still has X from the first trip' Legendaries); coolers (cool box/cooler/ice chest: 'kept it cold' Epics); coins (cash box/donation box rattle and overflow); cufflink/cufflinks (lost partner, wedding glitter); ring/wedding ring (slips off washing up); keepsake/storage/cigar/tin box ('kept the family's memories'); umbrellas ('keeps dry/cool' at three rarities).
patterns.suggestion: Per-id issues say which side to change. Give each sibling its own distinguishing trait (belt bag = hiking, bum bag = fashion/holiday, fanny pack = running; ice chest = fish, cooler = wheels, cool box = beach).

patterns.pattern: Matches: the Rare, Epic and Legendary celebrate lighting candles, lanterns and campfires, and are near-copies of w09 x_lighter and x_zippo. Child safety.
patterns.suggestion: Keep fire in the grown-up/high-shelf register: refusing to light for children, pick-up sticks, staying safely in the box. No move name about striking.

patterns.pattern: Near-copies of earlier drafts (mostly w07 clothing).

Jewellery sparkle frame: Rares and Epics are 'sparkled so brightly that...' (anklet, cufflink, ring, wedding ring, button, sequin, pendant, brooch, clutch, compact, hair slide). One sparkle line per sub-family is plenty.
patterns.suggestion: Use other real traits: clasps, tangling, turning fingers green, getting stuck, swinging, catching on fabric.

patterns.pattern: Ultimates repeat the Epic monster name plus Daze/Finale/Pong/Haul, sometimes promising stun where variants do not stun.
patterns.suggestion: Give the finisher its own image and keep it effect-neutral when the variants differ.

patterns.pattern: Legendary name shape monoculture: about two thirds are 'Old Xworth/Xwell of the Y' or 'Lady/Madame/Sir/Captain X of the Y'.
patterns.suggestion: Vary shapes: single coined names, 'X the Y' epithets, titles without 'of the'. The per-id replacements already vary some.

patterns.pattern: Move names padded with repeated words to dodge collisions ('Clasp Clasp Clasp Clasp', 'Glint Glint Glint Glint', 'Zip Pocket Crack Crack', 'Lid Snap Crack Snap', 'Pop Pop Pop Pop', 'Drip Drip Drip Drip', 'Tissue Tissue Tissue Tissue'). On single-hit moves a repeat falsely suggests multi-hit.
patterns.suggestion: Use a distinct image rather than an extra repeat.
